is: The app proper: a server-side `handleFetch` rewrite, a `$lib` split into an above-the-seam plain-data half and a below-the-seam Effect half, and the route tree (now with a dev-only mock signin endpoint under `routes/mock/`).
conventions: THE RUNES SEAM — Effect lives only under `lib/server/**`; `runApi` (`ManagedRuntime.runPromise`) is the one place programs become promises; loads/actions/components receive plain data and never see a fiber.
Generated protobuf types never cross the seam — they decode server-side and map to hand-written plain interfaces in `lib/api/`.
One-channel forms: values, field errors AND the backend Problem all ride the superform `message`.

Every response to a signed-in request (one carrying the `zurfur.sid` cookie `handleFetch` forwards) leaves `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`, set by the root `handle` hook — pages, 404/error pages and form-action JSON alike; no page can weaken it. The one exception is a redirect the sign-in gate throws: SvelteKit builds it outside the hook chain, so it leaves bare (a bodiless 303, which no cache stores without explicit freshness). Anonymous responses are untouched.

Errors never show their own message: the error pages pick their words by status and route from a fixed list (`error-copy.ts`), `error(status, message)` takes only a literal (lint-enforced; a message still ships in the page source), and `handleError` logs only the route template and status.
Every response carries `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'` and `X-Frame-Options: DENY` (a redirect the sign-in gate throws is the one bodiless exception).

fs.name: app.d.ts
fs.role: ambient types; App.Superforms.Message = Problem declared once

fs.name: hooks.server.spec.ts
fs.role: specs for the hooks — handle stamps the session and anti-framing headers and refuses a crafted (session) data request before it resolves; handleError is wired to the route-only logger; handleFetch, driven through SvelteKit's real server fetch (kit internals, on purpose), sends only zurfur.sid upstream

fs.name: hooks.server.ts
fs.role: handle — one chain (lib/server/handle-chain.ts): every response refuses framing (frame-headers.ts); every signed-in response leaves Cache-Control: private, no-store and Referrer-Policy: same-origin (session-headers.ts); every (session) load, data request and action requires a session (session-gate.ts); handleError — logs an unexpected error by route template and status only, fixed message to the page (error-log.ts); handleFetch — points same-origin /api/v1/* at the internal axum origin during SSR, forwards the session cookie

fs.name: lib/
fs.role: shared code, split above/below the runes seam

fs.name: routes/
fs.role: the SvelteKit route tree (includes a dev-only mock signin under routes/mock/)

notes: hooks.server.ts — the boot-time mock-mode guard: Checked at BOOT (not lazily on first request, unlike an earlier revision that lived in `runtime.ts`) so a misconfigured server fails to start rather than serving one request before crashing. Misconfiguration = `ZURFUR_WEB_MOCK` requested AND NOT a dev build AND NOT `vite build`'s own postbuild `building` phase (that carve-out keeps `ZURFUR_WEB_MOCK=1 yarn build` green when the flag leaks in from a dotenv-loaded `.env`, since `just`'s `dotenv-load` applies to every recipe, not only `dev-mock`). Loopback assumption stated once: mock mode is safe only because `vite dev` binds `127.0.0.1` by default — never pair `just dev-mock` with `--host`. `throw` is otherwise banned in production code (errors are values), but there is no request in flight yet at boot to carry one, so this is the one exception.

See also: internal ruling "9b" — `/` is the signed-in landing page after login/logout (cited in `routes/(public)/page.svelte.spec.ts`, `routes/(public)/login/+page.server.ts`); not yet a recorded DD, ask the Engineer if this should become one.
